chunks: And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said:
“The one suffering from an abdominal illness and the one with broken bones are to perform tayammum and are not to be given ghusl (ritual bathing).”

key_terms.الصَّادِقُ: Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام
key_terms.الْكَسِيرُ: a person with broken bones or serious fracture
key_terms.الْمَبْطُونُ: a person afflicted with a severe abdominal illness
key_terms.يُؤَمَّمَانِ: the two should perform tayammum (dry ablution)
key_terms.يُغَسَّلَانِ: the two are not to perform ghusl (ritual bathing)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on tayammum for a sick or injured person who cannot perform ghusl (ritual bathing)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for cases in which using water is harmful or unsuitable due to illness or injury. It establishes tayammum as the prescribed substitute and indicates that ghusl (ritual bathing) is not to be performed in such circumstances.
